description:
deviation.rs:354-580 represents DeviationScope as { kind: String, props: Vec<(String, ScopePropValue)> } instead of a closed Rust enum with one variant per canonical kind.

Defense: the closed-enum shape (the pre-PKIX-9vnx.11 design) forced every new scope axis to be a breaking change. The open-ended shape lets future axes (PolicyOid, SubjectDnContains, etc., tracked under PKIX-8mzp) land as new SCOPE_KIND_* constants without growing the enum. fail-closed on unknown kinds + validate_scope at insertion preserves correctness on both sides.

The trade is type-safety: the open shape admits malformed scopes at the type-system level, validated at runtime by validate_scope. DeviationAddError::MalformedScope surfaces the validation error so the operator sees a specific message rather than a silent never-match.

What a contributor might suggest changing: 'collapse this back to an enum, the open form sacrifices type safety'. Counter-argument: every canonical kind ships with a typed constructor (any / issuer_dn_contains / issuer_dn_exact / serial_range) — those preserve type safety at the construction boundary. validate_scope handles the residual hand-built-malformed case. The breaking-change cost of a closed enum is not worth the type-system gain.

Lock this in.
title: DeviationScope open-ended kind + props bag (PKIX-9vnx.11)
